title: U.S. Half Marathon Championship organisers offer $39k compensation to runners led off course
content:
Runners who followed a vehicle off course while leading the race at the USATF Half Marathon Championships will be given compensatory prize money by race organisers.

Jess McClain had been leading the field with under two miles remaining, followed by Emma Grace Hurley and Ednah Kurgat, before they were led off course by a race motorbike.

All three runners were forced to double back after the wrong turn.

Then-leader McClain finished ninth (1:11:27), behind eventual winner Molly Born (1:09:43) who had been more than a minute off her pace at the time of the diversion. Hurley and Kurgat finished 12th (1:11:38) and 13th (1:11:50) respectively.

Race organisers Atlanta Track Club admitted full responsibility for the mistake at the time and on Tuesday committed to match their lost prize money. McClain will receive $20,000 while Hurley and Kurgat will receive half of the combined total of second and third place, $9,500 each.

In their statement, the track club explained that the motorbike’s turn off course had been due to an incident of an officer being “struck by a vehicle” and taken to hospital, leading to a relocation of officers.

“The lead vehicle driver for the women’s race knew the course was to continue over the footbridge,” Atlanta Track Club said. “But because the intersection and the traffic cones had not been reset for the race due to the arrival of emergency vehicles, the driver followed a police motorcycle off course – believing the race was being rerouted.”

The championship on Sunday was a selection event for the September world championship event in Denmark, meaning McClain missed out on an automatic qualification spot alongside the chance to win her first national championship title.

USATF released a statement saying, however, that “the team is not officially selected until May” and they will “review the events from Atlanta carefully”.

Race winner Molly Born said after the event on her social media that she does “not feel like the winner of the 2026 USATF Half Marathon Championships, because I know I should not actually be the winner”.

Born also called for the three who had been leading the race to represent the U.S. in Denmark. “If a spot on the world team for Copenhagen is offered to me,” she continued. “I do not plan to take it regardless of who it goes to because I did not fairly earn it.”
